 JUDGMENT:
These claim petitions emanate in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioners by name Akshaya and Bhagyashree in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 13.08.2023.
2.

Since both these Petitions arise out of the same accident and in view of the Order dated 20.09.2024 in MVC No.6372/2023, these two cases were clubbed together and SCCH 15 3 MVC No.6372 & 6373/2023 taken for common disposal.

3. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 13.08.2023 at about 5.00 a.m., when the Petitioner in MVC No.6372/2023 was riding his two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-55-X-3671 along with pillion rider who is the Petitioner in MVC No.6373/2023 on Ramanjaneya road, Srinagara,
Bengaluru, at that time, driver of the TATA Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA-08-M-3213 (herein after referred to as offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, endangering human life and came on wrong lane and dashed against the petitioners vehicle.
Due to the said impact, both Petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
4. Immediately after the accident, the injured were shifted to KIMS hospital, after first aid both were shifted to Vasavi hospital, wherein they took treatment as inpatients.
Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- each SCCH 15 4 MVC No.6372 & 6373/2023 with cost and 18% interest in the interest of justice and equity.
5. In pursuance of service of the notice issued, the respondents have put in appearance and respondent No.1 has not filed any written statement.
Respondent No.2 has contested the petition and filed written statement.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 denies that it has issued insurance policy to the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.1 and denied liability to indemnify respondent Bhagyashree U K vs Venkoba Rao M on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86621062/

10. Issue No.1 in MVC No. 6372/2023 and 6373/2023 :- Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.
It is the contention of the petitioners that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA-08-M-3213 / offending vehicle.

11. In this regard the petitioner in MVC No.6372/2023 and petitioner in MVC No.6373/2023 have got themselves examined as PW.1 and 2 and in their chief examination they have deposed that on 13.08.2023 at about 5.00 a.m., Akshaya was riding a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-55-X-3671 along with with his friend on Ramanjaneya road, Srinagara, SCCH 15 8 MVC No.6372 & 6373/2023 Bengaluru, at that time, driver of the offending vehicle drove in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, endangering human life and came on wrong lane and dashed against the petitioners vehicle.
Due to the said impact, both Petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
12. The petitioners in support of their claim have in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to ExP15 documents.

Ex.P7 is the FIR registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint given by PW.1 as per Ex.P8 on 13.08.2023, hence there is no delay in lodging the complaint.
Ex . P9

-spot mahazar and sketch describes the spot of the accident and discloses that the accident has taken place on middle of the junction road and accident spot is the junction of Ramanjaneya road and 14th main road.
Ex.P13 is the IMV report which discloses the damages sustained in the accident.
Ex.P15 is the charge sheet filed after completion of the investigation SCCH 15 9 MVC No.6372 & 6373/2023 against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.

Hence, on the basis of these documents produced by the petitioners it is satisfactorily established that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

13. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 and 2 are cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination of PW.1 he has deposed that he was going along with his bike and he has produced his DL and stated that accident occurred at 5.00 p.m., and he was proceeding from Srinagara to Yalahanka to drop PW.2.
He has deposed that accident occurred in the middle of the road and denied that accident occurred due to his negligence.

PW.1 and 2 have clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 and 2 have stood unrebutted and PW1 and 2 have withstood the cross- examination of Respondent No.2.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioners in both cases and in the 'Affirmative'.

In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

15. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

As far as the medical bills are concerned petitioner has examined MRO of Vasavi hospital and he has produced inpatient case sheet and examined PW.4 who is the MRO of KIMS hospital and he has produced MLC extract, Inpatient case sheet along with X-rays which are marked at Ex.P49 to 54.

Ex. P4

Except suggesting that the said bills are created,
nothing is elicited to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.
Hence in view of Ex.P4 & 18 petitioner is awarded an amount of Rs.3,60,226/- under this head.
16. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents and ExP10 the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and petitioner cannot do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to the petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc.,
an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this SCCH 15 13 MVC No.6372 & 6373/2023 head.

The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit he has permanent disability and as per the evidence of PW.5 his impairment is not progressive and will not improve in future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that he cannot pursue his work as before the accident.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence, on the basis of these documents produced by the petitioners it is satisfactorily established that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of petitioners nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 and 2 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence on the part of petitioners.
PW.1 and 2 have clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 and 2 have stood unrebutted and PW1 and 2 have withstood the cross- examination of Respondent No.2.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR,
charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily SCCH 15 11 MVC No.6372 &
6373/2023 established that PW.1 and 2 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver, driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to the petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

is awarded to her towards pain and sufferings.

Hence, if the said disability is taken to the whole body it is just and proper to take it as 1/3 to the whole body.
